children: rises 4.2% in Monday's trading as J.P. Morgan initiated the development stage uranium company with an Overweight rating and $14 price target, saying the shares offer an attractive risk-reward profile backed by the scale, ultra-high grade, and low-cost nature of its flagship Rook I project.
JPM analyst Bill Peterson said NexGen's

"portfolio screens favorably in terms of grade (greater than 2% U3O8), scale (greater than 10% market share) and jurisdiction (Canada)," and that unlike peers, the project is fully permitted and well-supported by funding providers.
Rook I has the largest production and lowest all-in sustaining cost profile relative to peers under global coverage, and NextGen's

net present value sensitivity to uranium is relatively modfest compared to many high-torque upstream peers, reflecting the lowest-cost nature of the project, Peterson said, and "we see a path to a multi-decade mine life as adjacent prospects are integrated into the mine plan."

While construction is not without risk, Peterson said he sees headline risk as "longer-dated and valuation as undemanding, resulting in an attractive risk-reward" despite "superior asset quality and long-dated growth optionality."

title: NexGen Energy jumps as J.P. Morgan initiates at Overweight on flagship uranium project
